summary: Initial POC scoping for NovaHealth focused on how PII will be handled during a 6-week proof-of-concept. Key concerns: prompt storage, redaction at ingestion, configurable retention windows, audit logs for compliance, and workload sizing for latency & cost targets. Redwood AE/SE explained hosted vs private deployment trade-offs and suggested benchmarks (100k daily tokens, 95th p99 latency targets). Next steps include redwood sending security docs and customer providing sample prompts and traffic metrics.
topics: Audit logs and evidence for compliance
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-08-21
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Alvarez (Redwood SE), Aisha Rahman (Head of Data - NovaHealth), Tom Berger (CTO), Leila Park (Compliance)

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everyone thanks for joining. quick roll call?
[00:08] Aisha: Hi this is Aisha, from data team at NovaHealth. thanks for setting this up.
[00:12] Tom: Tom here, CTO. Leila from compliance will jump in with questions.
[00:18] Leila: hi all.
[00:20] Sofia: Great. Miguel from our infra team is here as well - he'll own sizing and the benchmark plan. miguel?
[00:26] Miguel: hey y'all. will try to keep it practical.

[00:35] Sofia: Objective for today: scope the POC's data handling requirements — specifically PII/redaction, prompt storage, and retention windows — and align on success criteria and preliminary sizing. Aisha, can you give a short picture of the workload?
[00:48] Aisha: Sure. NovaHealth runs a triage assistant integrated into our EMR frontend. PII includes patient names, dates, med IDs; requests are about 40k API calls per day now but expected to spike in POC to ~100k tokens/day because we'll attach clinical notes. Our main ask is: can we run a 6-week POC where data is not stored beyond a short window unless agreed, and we need audit logs for every inference for compliance review. also latency matters — clinicians need sub-600ms 95th percentile ideally.
[01:20] Miguel: quick clarification — 100k tokens/day or 100k requests?
[01:24] Aisha: 100k tokens/day roughly, maybe 10-15k requests. most requests will be short but some will include 1-2KB of clinical text.

[01:36] Sofia: thanks. Leila, are there any must-have controls?
[01:40] Leila: yes, we need clear proof that PII isn't retained by default. our security team will want: SAML SSO for console access, KMS-backed key management for any stored artifacts, and exportable audit logs (immutable) for a time window we define. during POC we can accept 30-day logs but production may be longer. also data residency — all processing must be in us-east-1 for now.
[02:05] Miguel: noted. we can pin region and we support KMS integrations. one question from our side: do you need the model to see raw prompts verbatim for benchmarking, or can we provide redacted samples?
[02:18] Aisha: we need both. for quality checks we'll need verbatim prompts, but for legal we need a redaction pipeline. ideally Redwood can show an ingestor that redacts before storage while still allowing ephemeral use in the runtime.
[02:32] Sofia: good point. so two parallel tracks: (A) ephemeral inference where prompt is used in-flight and not persisted, and (B) configurable persistence with redaction applied before storage. Miguel will map the options.

[02:45] Leila: can you tell me how Redwood does redaction? is it client-side or server-side? any human review?
[02:53] Miguel: current pattern is flexible — we offer SDK-level hooks so customers can apply client-side redaction before sending, or send raw and let server-side preprocessor run deterministic redaction rules (PII regex, name lists). server-side redaction can be run before writing to logs/storage. for POC we propose server-side with telemetry that shows redaction hits; if that is sensitive we can do client-side. human review is not part of our default flow unless you enable it.
[03:20] Leila: okay and about encryption at rest and in transit?
[03:24] Sofia: TLS in transit, and AES-256 at rest; for extra control we support bringing your own KMS keys.

[03:30] Tom: what's the retention configuration look like? we might want short-term prompt retention to support debugging early POC issues but then flip to ephemeral. how flexible?
[03:40] Miguel: retention is configurable per-tenant and per-route. you can set prompt retention to 0 (never stored), 1 day, 7 days, 30 days, or a custom TTL. we also have a scrubbed/pseudonymized storage option where certain fields are masked before storage.

[03:56] Aisha: for the POC let's propose 14-day retention for logs and 0-day retention for raw prompts by default. we'll provide a small set of flagged prompts that we allow Redwood to keep longer for debugging.
[04:06] Sofia: sounds reasonable. we'll document that as part of the POC template.

[04:12] Miguel: on benchmarking — typical measures we suggest: token throughput per GPU, p95/p99 latency for your payload distribution, and quality delta vs your current baseline. given the 1-2KB payloads some inference modes might benefit from KV cache hits but this is less relevant for short-lived clinical prompts. we should run two bench scenarios: baseline (no redaction, full fidelity) and redaction-before-storage scenario to measure processing overhead.
[04:42] Tom: and can we run it in a VPC/private deployment? data residency plus compliance might push us that way.
[04:49] Sofia: yes — Redwood Private gives a customer-managed VPC option. for POC we can do either: hosted in us-east-1 with strict controls or a dedicated private tenant in your VPC. Private will add setup time. Miguel, estimate how long to stand up a private tenant for a 6-week POC?
[05:04] Miguel: with automation, initial infra and connectivity usually takes 10-14 business days if networking and KMS are ready. if we need on-prem air-gapped installs that's longer. For hosted with VPC peering we can do 2-3 business days typically.

[05:18] Leila: so timeline matters. we have a compliance review mid-September, so POC needs to start first week of September. can you meet that?
[05:27] Sofia: we're close but that pushes us. hosted POC starting Sept 2 is doable. private POC start Sept 8 likely but depends on your infra team's readiness.

[05:36] Aisha: success criteria — we need a list. I'll propose: 1) end-to-end workflow with clinician UX under 600ms p95, 2) redaction shows >99% of PII patterns for our sample set, 3) audit logs show per-inference evidence and KMS-controlled keys, 4) throughput meets 100k tokens/day at acceptable cost. Any additions?
[05:56] Miguel: add a quality pass: model outputs must match baseline correctness within X% on the shared eval set — we can define X with you, maybe 95% of current accuracy on core triage labels.
[06:08] Tom: and cost estimate target? we need a projected monthly cost if we expand. rough ballpark is fine.
[06:13] Sofia: we'll produce a cost model tied to the benchmark results. I'll include cost per 1M tokens for hosted vs per-GPU-hour for dedicated.

[06:20] [06:20] interruption - brief cross-talk, unclear
[06:26] Miguel: on measurement — for p95 numbers we need realistic payload distribution. Aisha, can you send a CSV of 24h of traffic sample (anonymized or redacted) so we can synthesize the bench?
[06:36] Aisha: yes we'll do that. we might need help anonymizing before sending.
[06:41] Leila: we prefer to keep anything PHI out. can Redwood run an on-prem redaction step?
[06:48] Miguel: yes we can provide a small dockerized preprocessor for local redaction — runs with your keys and never leaves your network; the output is a synthetic set we can use for bench. that's typically the safest route.

[06:59] Sofia: good. I'll add that as an option in the runbook.

[07:04] Aisha: about audit logs — what fields are included? we need timestamp, route, model version, redaction status, KMS key id, and hash of the prompt for traceability without storing raw text.
[07:18] Miguel: we can include all those. we also support storing a one-way SHA-256 hash of prompts — matches on your side but not reversible. logs are exportable in NDJSON for your SIEM.

[07:30] Leila: will logs be immutable? we need write-once retention for compliance.
[07:34] Miguel: yes we can push to an immutable bucket or a WORM-backed store for the POC, or export to your existing logging infra.

[07:42] Sofia: any blockers on Redwood's side? none immediate. we'll need the sample data and a decision hosted vs private.

[07:50] Tom: one more technical: does Redwood's runtime do prompt-level redaction before tokenization, or after? some patterns need tokenization-aware masking.
[08:00] Miguel: currently pre-tokenization — regex and ML-based detectors run on the raw text. we can also plug in token-aware scrubbers if you want match across token boundaries, but that requires an extra pipeline step. for POC we suggest starting with regex + name lists and measure false negatives.

[08:18] Aisha: what's the expected overhead for server-side redaction?
[08:23] Miguel: usually small: 20-80ms per request depending on text length and detectors. we'll measure this in the benchmark.

[08:32] Sofia: fine. let's outline the bench plan: 1) get 24h traffic sample (Aisha), 2) Redwood creates synthetic bench suite and runs baseline hosted tests (Miguel), 3) run redaction-on-ingest scenario and measure delta, 4) provide cost and sizing report and recommendations for quantization/caching. target turnaround 5 business days once sample is in. Sound good?
[08:57] Aisha: yes.

[09:00] Leila: can you share security docs now? SOC2, encryption, redaction whitepaper?
[09:07] Sofia: yes we'll attach SOC2 summary and a short redaction whitepaper. I'll include the RBAC/SSO checklist.

[09:15] Tom: any remarks re: competitors? we're evaluating other vendors but main differentiator is dev velocity and control.
[09:22] Sofia: understood. we'll highlight the Private and audit capabilities.

[09:28] Miguel: quick note: if you go private we can also enable local-only persistence keys and tighter log routing which helps compliance.

[09:36] Aisha: that's attractive.

[09:40] Sofia: OK final recap: deliverables from Redwood: security pack + redaction whitepaper, retention templates, sizing spreadsheet after sample, bench plan and cost model. Customer deliverables: sample prompts/24h traffic (anonymized), decision hosted vs private, list of PII patterns. We'll reconvene after benchmark results.

[09:58] Leila: thanks everyone.
[10:00] Sofia: thanks, we'll send notes and next steps. meeting ends.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mislabels and dropped words; speaker overlap at 06:20 clip.
